Use case: stylized-concept. NEW COMPOSITION of an original goofy 2D football club hub, landscape 16:10. Input 1 is the previous cartoon yard, provided ONLY for its bold ink, vivid teal/mustard/coral colors and hilarious distorted football architecture; DO NOT reuse its composition. Input 2 is our player portrait sheet, only for drawing-language consistency. Keep the sports-caricature attitude and squash-and-stretch shapes inspired by Tape to Tape. Original artwork. Cartoon drawing with BELIEVABLE SPATIAL ORGANIZATION, not realistic rendering.
The crucial request: a coherent, lived-in football club compound with STRONG DEPTH and natural building placement. A slightly elevated camera looks DIAGONALLY THROUGH THE ENTRANCE into the grounds. ONE continuous ground plane. Consistent receding perspective. Near objects visibly larger, distant objects smaller; genuine partial occlusion and overlapping silhouettes. Buildings vary in angle, depth and size. No rows, no 3-by-3 arrangement, no equal-sized attractions, no separated display podiums, no frontal catalogue of props.
FOREGROUND: a cropped fence and open gate frame the lower corners. A very large battered scouting minivan with comically mismatched monster tyres is parked OBLIQUELY at lower right along the near service drive, its near wheel partly cropped. Its body recedes toward the center, luggage and huge map on bonnet. A curved entrance drive starts bottom center, goes behind the clubhouse, then narrows toward the stadium entrance in the upper-right distance. This drive and a narrower branch to the training ground establish the perspective, not arbitrary platform paths.
MIDGROUND LEFT: the main changing-room clubhouse is the dominant nearby building, an irregular connected L-shaped complex, roof and side wall visible. It has a hilariously sagging red roof, a boot-shaped changing-room wing with an open locker-room door showing a hanging green football shirt, and a giant whistle chimney. The building partially blocks the structures behind it; do NOT separate its wings into individual standalone stalls. On its front porch, near the viewer, sit a modest stack of blank newspapers, an old dark blank-screen TV with silly referee-flag aerials, and a purple VHS box, integrated under ONE shared awning. Each of these 3 objects must remain visible and distinct for UI hit targets. An open trophy window on the front-facing wall displays a ridiculously oversized golden boot and small trophy, naturally part of this clubhouse rather than a giant outdoor standalone trophy stall.
FURTHER BACK: a smaller admin annex is physically connected behind the clubhouse on its right; visible office window with an exaggerated calculator and files. Leave its entrance/window distinguishable despite overlap. A training-ground fence recedes behind the clubhouse. A crooked chalk tactics board with simple pitch marks and a small bench stands beside the path at the training entrance, facing the field, not centered like an exhibition booth.
BACKGROUND: a full training pitch runs away from the viewer behind the near clubhouse, with 3 oversized cartoon orange cones and a training goal, fence lines converge strongly. In the far upper-right is the main football stadium, substantial in real scale but smaller on screen through distance: drooping grandstand roof, football-shaped entrance arch, bent floodlights. Trees and low hills beyond help depth but remain flat cartoon shapes.
The important readable interactive landmarks are changing door, training pitch, stadium entrance, chalkboard, admin window, van, newspaper stack, TV, VHS crate and trophy window. They are NOT arranged as a grid. Some buildings and fence edges are naturally cut off by the frame, but keep every interactive landmark visibly clickable. Give space to the circulation route; the facility layout must look usable by an actual football club.
Thick expressive navy ink, simplified broad cel colors, playful wonky football silhouettes, hard shadow shapes only. No people, lettering, labels, UI, words or numbers, no photorealism, realistic textures, fine foliage, 3D lighting or painterly scenic detail. Keep the outrageous cartoon style while using realistic compound planning and perspective.

Use case: stylized-concept. Original production environment for an OUTRAGEOUS cartoon football management game. Landscape 16:10. INPUT 1 is our player's flat-ink portrait sheet and INPUT 2 is our new absurd clubhouse yard: match its punchy dark ink, wild squash-and-stretch architecture and slapstick scale, with the irreverent sports comedy energy of Tape to Tape. Original artwork, no existing characters. Bold 7-10px outer contours, lively thin internal linework, flat cel color, mustard, coral, teal and small violet accents. Every prop has a funny silhouette, aggressively lopsided, stretched or squashed. No plausible conservative room design. NO realistic lighting or materials, gradients, 3D, painterly detail or precious rustic scenery. NO humans, portraits, letters, numerals, logos or interface panels.
A surreal football team's changing room, straight-on shallow perspective, as if built inside the enormous football-boot-shaped clubhouse. The middle 80% of the scene from y25% to y76% MUST be a clean uninterrupted mostly empty deep teal wall; only 4 or 5 giant warped wall panels, so real interactive lockers and player portraits will be placed on top. Do NOT draw lockers in this reserved region.
The upper 22% is hilarious: the ceiling droops like an exhausted hammock, a giant brass whistle-shaped ventilation pipe sticks in at upper left, two comically pinched tiny skewed windows, a football-shaped clock swollen 3 times normal size leaning at upper right with blank face and two hands, fat bent water pipes that tie themselves in a loose knot at the far right edge. A ginormous rolled sock hangs limply off the far right pipe. Far left edge a crooked door with enormous coach clipboard and absurdly tiny pencil, visible at edge only.
Along the BOTTOM 18% an exaggerated bowed yellow wooden bench sags under the weight of ONE gigantic battered football boot at far left. Its shoelace is tangled in a football. Far right a tiny shower door almost covered by a ludicrously long striped towel that puddles on the floor. Floor tiles are oversized wobbly terracotta trapezoids. Simple central wall to keep roster readable, comedy concentrated at ceiling, far sides and bottom. Exaggeration 10/10, very chunky graphic silhouettes, bold lively line. No text and no people.
